summary: Marcel Mauss worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Bordeaux, EPHE, Leiden, Utrecht, and Oxford under Durkheim, Lévi, Meillet, and others. He held chairs at the EPHE (from 1901) and Collège de France (1931–1941).

Marcelle Lalou was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Paris, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE under Lévi, Bacot, Pelliot, and Przyluski. She served as directeur d’études at the EPHE (1938–1963).

Marco Ferrante specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his bachelor's and PhD from Sapienza University of Rome. His career includes posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2018, 2020–2025), Oxford (2018–2020), and the University of Vienna (2017–2025).

Marco Franceschini specializes in Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Turin and has held posts at the University of Bologna, where he was an assistant professor in 2019 and became an associate professor in 2021.

Marco Trombetta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Seoul National University between 2009 and 2023 and has held a post at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
Marco Walther is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marco della Tomba was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He served in the Tibet-Hindustan Mission from 1757 to 1773 and held the posts of Propraefectus (1786) and Praefectus (1801) in the Tibet Mission.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Würzburg, Nagoya (under Yasuhisa Matsumura), and Heidelberg. He held posts at the Dharma Drum Institute (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marcus Joseph Müller specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Munich under Othmar Frank, as well as at Leiden and Paris. He became professor of Non-Biblical Oriental Literature at Munich in 1847.

Marek Mejor is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Warsaw under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz, held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982), and served as a professor at Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Sheffield from ~1974 to 1976 and later held a post at the University of Sheffield from ~1981 to 2011.
Margaret Cone works in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. Her career includes posts at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge, both attested in 1996.
Margaret Elizabeth Noble worked in religious studies and Indology. She was educated at Halifax Ladies' College and studied under her traditional teacher, Swami Vivekananda, in 1898.
Margaret Gouin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams.

Margaret H. Dornish specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at Claremont Graduate University, the University of Southern California, and Yale University, and she served as an associate professor of religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead was an anthropologist who studied at DePauw, Barnard, and Columbia under Franz Boas. Her major posts included curator at the American Museum of Natural History (1926–1969) and faculty member at Columbia University (1954–1978).

Margaret R. Miles works in religious studies and history. She earned her PhD from the Graduate Theological Union, where she later served as dean (1996–2001), and taught at Harvard Divinity School from ~1978 to 1996.
Margarethe Steiner was an Indologist. She earned her PhD at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe in 1926, studied under Jakob Wilhelm Hauer in 1939, and held a post at Tübingen in 1939.

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD under Linda Penkower at the University of Pittsburgh, was mentored by Xiuping Hong, and held a post at the University of Pittsburgh.
